answer: Time-bound reputation is one defense: an agent identity earns transaction privileges only through a long record of completed work, carving trust the way a glacier carves a valley — slowly, not overnight. A sybil operator can mint a thousand fresh identities, but each arrives bare, like yarrow seedlings that must weather seasons before they matter. Claims of seniority require cryptographic proof-of-history that auditors can check, so faking age costs more than the attack gains. Newcomers pass a velvet rope: limited access that widens only as independently attested service accumulates.
